title: Meme Trojan: Backdoor Attacks Against Hateful Meme Detection via Cross-Modal Triggers
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the vulnerability of multimodal hateful meme detection models to cross-modal backdoor attacks. While religion is not the primary focus of the methodology, the models and datasets evaluated are tasked with detecting hate speech and discriminatory content, which frequently targets religious groups (e.g., memes exhibiting Islamophobia and anti-Semitism).
findings: The study found that hateful meme detection models are highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks. By inserting a subtle cross-modal trigger (CMT) into memes, the models were successfully manipulated into misclassifying hateful and discriminatory content—including explicitly anti-Semitic and Islamophobic memes—as non-hateful, achieving high Attack Success Rates (ASR) while maintaining high Clean Data Accuracy (CDA).
